sentences.text: 2  JUDGMENT MFA No.201464/2019 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - XII, Vijaypur (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.2198/2014 vide its judgment and award dated 17.01.2019.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - XII, Vijaypur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. MFA No.201598/2019 is filed by the insurer challenging the finding regarding the involvement of the offending vehicle as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the aforesaid claim petition.
3. A claim petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by the claimant in a road accident on 21.09.2014.

The claimant claimed that on the said day, he was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-15/BT-7319 which was dashed against by a car bearing registration No.MH-13/N-0670 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle').

As a result of the impact, the claimant was thrown off the motorcycle and suffered serious injuries on the face, lower limb and dislocation on the left side and cut lacerated wound on the right little NC: 2023:KHC-K:5509 finger and right ring finger and other wounds on the dorsal side of the right hand.
He claimed that he was treated as an inpatient at Ashwini Sahakari Rugnalaya and Research Center, Solapur.

entities.text: Ashwini Sahakari Rugnalaya and Research Center, Solapur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He claimed that he was 30 years old and was an agriculturist earning Rs.7,500/- per month.
He claimed that due to the injuries sustained, he was disabled and could no longer undertake any agricultural activity.
4. The claim petition was resisted by the owner who denied the averments contained therein.
He denied that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
He also denied the age, income of the claimant as well as the injuries suffered by him.
The insurer also denied the averments of the claim petition.
It also denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It denied the injuries suffered by the claimant as well as the expenses incurred for his treatment.
It contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence and therefore, the owner of the offending vehicle had entrusted a vehicle to an unauthorized person.
Hence, it claimed that conditions of policy of insurance was violated.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P17.
He examined a Doctor as PW.2, who deposed based on the medical records that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body and 30% to 40% to the limb.

The insurer examined driver of the offending vehicle as RW.1 and one of its official as RW.2 and marked Exs.R1 to R3.
6.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that RW.1 being the driver of the offending vehicle did admit that he had dashed against the motorcycle ridden by the claimant.
It also considered other documents marked by the claimant and held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

In so far as quantum of Mallinath vs Mrs Mukta A And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149416891/
3 compensation is concerned, it held that the claimant had suffered comminuted fracture of right tibia and other wounds over the little finger and ring finger of the right hand, multiple abrasion over right dorsum side of the right hand.

sentences.text: It also considered that the claimant was admitted on 29.09.2014 and discharged on 17.11.2014.

It considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of NC:
2023:KHC-K:5509 Rs.5,000/- per month and disability was assessed at 12% to the whole body and the following compensation was awarded:-

 1 Injury, pain and sufferings 20,000/-

Medical expenses 6,88,600/-
 3 Loss of income due to permanent 1,22,400/-
 physical disability  4 Food and nourishment charges 10,000/-

5 Attendant charges 10,000/-
 6 Conveyance charges 10,000/-
 7 Loss of amenities and future 20,000/-
 unhappiness  Total 8,81,000/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
7. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed MFA no.201464/2019.
Being aggrieved by the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation as well as the quantum of compensation, the insurer has filed MFA No.201598/2019.
The learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the claimant had not only suffered fracture of the tibia but suffered dislocation of the superior and inferior pubic rami as per Ex.P5.
He also suffered multiple facial fractures and also fracture of the neck of femur of the right leg.

Therefore,
the learned counsel contends that the claimant had suffered disability which was not properly assessed by the Tribunal.
He therefore, contends that the disability suffered by the claimant deserves to be properly assessed and enhanced taking into account the functional ability that it affected.
He further contended that the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.
He also contends that the compensation awarded under the other heads warrants enhancement.
9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer submitted that as per Ex.P16, hospital authorities have intimated the jurisdictional police that some unknown vehicle had knocked down the claimant.
He submits that in the absence of any evidence that the vehicle in question was involved in the accident, false charge-sheet was filed against the offending vehicle.
He further submits that there was no NC: 2023:KHC-K:5509 damage found on the car and therefore, the involvement of the car is doubtful.

He further submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is excessive as the Mallinath vs Mrs Mukta A And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149416891/
4 medical expenses awarded by the Tribunal is without any basis.
10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the insurer.
I have also perused the documents placed on record by the learned counsel for the claimant.
11. The records furnished by the learned counsel for the claimant discloses that the insurer had examined the driver of the car as RW.1.
This witness deposed that the car that he drove on the said day had dashed against the motorcycle ridden by the claimant.
Though this witness was treated as hostile, no evidence was extracted from this witness to establish that his evidence was false or that he had changed the side to favour the claimant.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident is justified.

12. In so far as quantum of compensation is concerned, Ex.P5 which is the discharge summary indicates that the claimant had not only suffered head injury with multiple facial NC:
2023:KHC-K:5509 fractures, he had also suffered fracture of neck of the femur of the right leg,
fracture of the tibia and dislocation of the superior and inferior pubic rami.
There is no contra evidence extracted from PW.2 to establish that Ex.P5, the discharge summary did not correspond with other medical records marked in the case.
In that view of the matter, taking into consideration the injuries suffered by the claimant, it is appropriate to consider the disability suffered by the claimant at 20% to the whole body.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimant, the notional income of the claimant ought to have been taken at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.

Therefore, the claimant was entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Injury, pain and sufferings 40,000/-
 2 Medical expenses 6,88,600/-
 3 Loss of income during the 22,500/-
 period of treatment for 3  months

4 Loss of income due to disability 3,06,000/-
 (7,500 x 12 x 17 x 20%)
5 Food, nourishment, conveyance 25,000/-
and attendant charges

6 Loss of amenities 40,000/-
 Total 11,22,100/-
 - 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5509 13.

In so for as contention of the insurer that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident,
the same is liable to be rejected in view of the evidence of RW.1.

Likewise, the contention of the insurer that the medical expenses awarded by the Tribunal was exorbitant and baseless, the medical Mallinath vs Mrs Mukta A And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149416891/
5 bills which are 207 in numbers clearly correspond with the discharge summaries issued as per Exs.P5 and P7.

entities.text: medical Mallinath vs Mrs Mukta A And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently this contention does not merit consideration.
14. In view of the above, the appeal filed by the claimant in MFA No.201464/2019 is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.8,81,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.11,22,100/-, which is payable by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

15. The compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer of the offending vehicle before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
17. The appeal filed by the insurer in MFA No.201598/2019 is dismissed.
18. The amount in deposit in MFA No.201598/2019 is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
